title: Sales Enablement: Prospect Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This prospect-facing playbook gathers the canonical positioning, competitive talking points, slide guidance, pricing reference, short case studies, and a concise Security FAQ for sales and solutions engineering use when engaging prospective customers. Use this doc during discovery, technical qualification, and executive pitch moments.

Audience and intended use

- Sales (AE/SDR) for executive and economic conversations
- Solutions Engineering for technical deep dives and security discussion
- Sales Engineers for pilots, POC scoping, and pricing guidance
- Customer Success for handoff language

Positioning & Messaging

Core one-liner
- Redwood Inference: A developer-first inference platform that makes production-grade LLM serving predictable, economical, and secure across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Value pillars (talking points)
- Production-first reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated options, multi-region fallbacks, and SLO observability for latency and error budgets.
- Predictable economics: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and operational UX across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes.
- Developer experience: fast onboarding, SDKs, streaming & function calling support, and per-route tracing.

Elevator pitch (30s)
- For engineering teams that need reliable, cost-effective LLM inference, Redwood provides a unified runtime and control plane to run models across hosted, reserved, or private infrastructure with measurable latency and unit-cost guarantees — without building custom serving stacks.

Proof points & evidence
- Performance: typical 95th percentile gen latency < 200ms for small-medium prompts on Dedicated with our default config (customer results vary by model and sequence length).
- Cost: customers report 20-50% TCO reduction vs unmanaged GPU fleets after enabling batching + KV caching and recommended quantization profile.
- Reliability: built-in routing policies and automatic fallbacks have reduced cross-service outages in pilot customers by 80%.

Competitive brief (one-page summary)

High-level competitor positioning
- Large cloud ML endpoints: easy to start, but lower transparency into serving economics and limited private deployment options at scale.
- LLM API providers: simple API and managed models; many trade off enterprise control and private deployment.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes: maximum control but high engineering cost to achieve SLOs, observability, and rollout tooling.

Quick comparison table (condensed)
| Capability | Redwood Inference | Cloud ML Endpoints | LLM API Providers | Self-hosted Runtime |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment modes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted / Managed | Hosted | Self-host only |
| Predictable unit cost | Yes (optimize + reporting) | Limited | Varies | Potentially, but engineering heavy |
| Private/VPC/on-prem | Yes (supported) | Limited | Rare | Yes |
| Observability & rollouts | Per-model/per-route dashboards + tracing | Basic monitoring | Varies | Custom built |
| Enterprise SLAs | Available (Dedicated) | Varies | Limited | Depends on org |

How to use vs each competitor (talking bullets)
- Against cloud ML endpoints: emphasize unit-cost control, batching and caching optimizations, and Private deployment options for regulated customers.
- Against LLM API providers: emphasize Dedicated and Private deployment modes and the ability to pin model versions and roll out safely.
- Against self-hosted runtime: emphasize time-to-production, integrated observability, and lower long-term total-cost-of-ownership.

Pitch deck guidance (recommended slide flow)

1. Title / Opening (1 slide)
- Customer logo + Redwood logo, one-line summary of value
2. Problem (1 slide)
- Bullet problems: unpredictable latency, exploding token costs, deployment ops burden, lack of enterprise controls
3. Redwood solution overview (1 slide)
- Diagram: API -> Smart routing & runtime -> Hosted/Dedicated/Private
4. Key differentiators (1 slide)
- Production-first, unified runtime, cost controls, private deployments
5. Performance & economics (1-2 slides)
- Typical latency and cost improvements seen in pilots (quantitative metrics)
6. Architecture & integrations (1 slide)
- Network, KMS, audit logging, identity (OIDC/SSO), VPC peering/Direct Connect
7. Security and compliance (1 slide)
- Certifications, audit logging, tenancy options, encryption at rest/in-transit
8. Pricing & commercial model (1 slide)
- Short summary of hosted usage, dedicated reserved capacity, private licensing + support
9. Pilot & success criteria (1 slide)
- Scope, POC length (2-6 weeks), success metrics (latency target, cost delta, throughput)
10. Case study highlights & references (1 slide)
11. Next steps & ask (1 slide)
- POC kickoff, technical contacts, legal/compliance checklist

Slide tips for SEs
- Keep technical slides concise: architecture diagrams with callouts for SLOs and integration points.
- Include one explicit "success metric" slide showing how the pilot will be measured.
- Hand the customer a short appendix with configuration examples (batching, quantization profile names).

Pricing guidance (concise reference)

Pricing model overview
- Hosted API: usage-based billing (per-token for generation and per-embedding for embeddings). Typical entry tier includes free trial credits.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly or annual reserved GPU capacity with commit levels and negotiated overage/burst rates. SLA options available.
- Private: platform license + deployment support and optional managed services (pricing typically annual, based on required capacity, support tier, and features).

Arranging price conversations
1. Discovery: collect estimated QPS, average prompt length, expected concurrency, retention/compliance needs, and preferred deployment mode.
2. Pricing tier recommendation: map expected usage to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Provide ballpark monthly TCO with 3 scenario buckets (low/expected/high).
3. Commercial motion: for deals above $50k ARR, engage Sales Engineering + Solutions Architect for a tailored Dedicated/Private proposal.

Negotiation playbook (common concessions & guardrails)
- Pilot discounts: offer time-limited pilot credits tied to success criteria (30-60 days).
- Ramp commitments: use graduated commit tiers with quarterly review windows.
- Professional services: scope clearly and price separately to avoid hiding engineering effort.

Sample pricing snippet (example only)
- Hosted: $0.0009 / input token, $0.0018 / output token (example; actual rates vary by model).
- Dedicated: reserved node bundles starting at $X,000 / month for N vGPUs + overage at Y% of commit.
- Private: platform license $Z,000 / year + onboarding & support.

Case studies (short, scannable)

Case study A: Conversational SaaS startup
- Problem: Erratic latency and high inference cost on generic cloud endpoints.
- Deployment: Dedicated with autoscaling + KV caching enabled.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in per-request cost, 40% improvement in 95th percentile latency, achieved within a 6-week integration.

Case study B: Regulated financial services pilot
- Problem: Required VPC-only deployment with strict audit logging and KMS integration.
- Deployment: Private VPC deployment with customer KMS + SSO integration.
- Outcome: Pilot completed in 8 weeks; compliance sign-off achieved and plan for Dedicated rollout.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for common questions)

Q: Where is data stored and how long is it retained?
A: For Hosted customers, request/response logs are retained per customer-configurable retention windows; default retention is 30 days for logs and 90 days for observability summaries. For Private/Dedicated, all persisted telemetry can be routed to customer-controlled storage.

Q: Can we use our KMS/HSM for key management?
A: Yes. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated deployments.

Q: How is PHI/PII protected?
A: We recommend Private/Dedicated deployments for regulated workloads. Data-at-rest and in-transit is encrypted (TLS 1.2+), access is RBAC-controlled, and audit logs are available to track dataset and request access.

Q: Do you perform model-level content filtering or data minimization?
A: Redwood offers configurable output filters and data redaction hooks in the runtime; customers can also configure prompt-side sanitization and on-the-wire filters in the proxy layer.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness for our control plane and provides evidence for enterprise customers. For private deployments we supply the artifacts required for customer audit.

Q: What network options do you support for Private deployment?
A: VPC peering, PrivateLink, Direct Connect/Cloud Interconnect, and customer-managed firewall policies.

Q: How are model versions managed and rolled out?
A: We support pinning to model versions, canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallbacks. All rollout events are logged and visible in the Console.

How to use this playbook (operational steps)

1. Early discovery: use the positioning bullets and elevator pitch.
2. Technical discovery: SE collects QPS/concurrency/prompt-length and security requirements.
3. Slide deck: follow the recommended flow and include success criteria.
4. Pilot scoping: propose a 2-6 week pilot with defined success metrics (latency & cost targets).
5. Handoff: after POC, include Customer Success with runbook for onboarding.
